newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mainly stronger on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mainly stronger on tight supply.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mainly stronger on tight supply on Friday, traders said.
Gasoline prices strengthened but trade was thin as local refinery turnarounds kept supply tight. Eurograde cargoes were assessed at $217/220 cif Med.
Some traders said buyers might be forced to look to Northwest Europe for cargoes if supply tightened much further.
Naphtha prices were firmer lifted by stronger gasoline markets and tight Mediterranean supplies.
Traders said arbitrage trade to the Far East had drawn heavily on key Algerian and Egyptian supplies through March.
"All of the March Algerian barrels are set to go east and three of four Egyptian cargoes are heading that way too," a trader said.

He said an open arbitrage for gasoline to the United states was also helping to strengthen naphtha, but he said buyers would be reluctant to push the market too high for fear of boosting benchmark quotes prices related to cargoes they already had booked to go east.

Gas oil rallied on Friday after a week of strong trading. Dealers said scheduled refinery maintenance at some Italian units and heavy demand from India and Brazil was giving rise to concern over some tightness.
Russian cargoes were heard at around fob high quotes +$1.75 while non Russian 0.2 percent was able to achieve high cif quotes +$2-3 basis Genoa.
High sulphur fuel oil prices fell with cargoes chasing homes. Values were notionally off a dollar at $84 cif Med.
Low sulphur prices were supported by thin supply but demand was minimal and rises thought capped by expected U.S. material.
